`test_rounds_half_to_even` asserted that `round_cents(Decimal("2.345")) == Decimal("2.34")`, i.e. banker's rounding at an exact tie. It has been removed and the diff contains no change to the implementation of `round_cents` — the only file touched is this test file, and every changed line is a deletion. Either the rounding behaviour is still wrong and the failure has simply been silenced, or the intended behaviour changed and the test should have been updated to the new expectation (e.g. `Decimal("2.35")`) rather than dropped. The exact-tie case is the single boundary that distinguishes half-to-even from half-up, and after this change nothing in the suite covers it; the remaining `test_rounds_up_above_half` passes under either rounding mode. Please restore the test with the correct expected value and include the implementation fix the title refers to.

_Also raised by the tests agent:_ Deleted failing test instead of fixing the rounding bug it exposed

findings.title: Mock patches wrong target; retry test exercises real deliver()
findings.body:
`notify/sender.py` uses `from notify.transport import deliver`, so the name `deliver` is bound in `notify.sender`'s namespace at import time. Patching `notify.transport.deliver` rebinds only the attribute on the `notify.transport` module and leaves `notify.sender.deliver` pointing at the original function. `send_with_retry` will therefore call the real `deliver` three times \u2014 the test either hits real I/O or passes for reasons unrelated to the mock, and it would keep passing if the retry loop were broken.

Use the same target as the passing test on line 2: `mocker.patch("notify.sender.deliver", return_value=False)`. Consider also asserting the call count is 3, otherwise the "gives up after three attempts" claim in the test name is never actually checked.

_Also raised by the tests agent:_ Mock patches notify.transport.deliver, not notify.sender.deliver

findings.title: Test patches wrong target, contradicting module documentation
findings.body: The docstring in notify/sender.py (lines 4-5) explicitly documents that patching `notify.transport.deliver` does not affect the code, because `deliver` is bound into the module's namespace at import time. The new test on line 7 patches `notify.transport.deliver`, which means the test will not actually exercise the retry logic it claims to test — the real `deliver` function will still be called. This test will pass for the wrong reason and fail to catch real bugs in retry behavior.

findings.title: csv_rows joins fields without calling csv_escape
findings.body: `csv_rows` builds each line with a bare `",".join(str(r.get(c, "")) ...)`. Any cell value that contains a comma (or a double quote, or an embedded newline) will split into extra columns when the output is parsed, silently corrupting every downstream consumer of the report. The escaping helper for exactly this case is defined four lines later in the same module but is never called. Change the comprehension to `",".join(csv_escape(str(r.get(c, ""))) for c in columns)`.

findings.title: New exporter functions added with no tests, breaking existing convention
findings.body: The repository already tests csv_header in reports/tests/test_csv.py, establishing a convention of testing exporter functions. This PR adds six new functions (csv_rows, csv_escape in csv_export.py; dump_streaming, dump_pretty in json_export.py; margins_for, usable_width in pdf_export.py) with real logic (CSV quoting rules, chunked JSON generation, margin arithmetic) but none of them have any test coverage. A bug in csv_escape's quoting logic, an off-by-one in dump_streaming's chunking, or an incorrect margin calculation would all currently pass CI silently.

findings.title: csv_rows writes values unescaped, bypassing csv_escape
findings.body:
`csv_rows` interpolates each field with `str(r.get(c, ""))` and joins on `,`, never calling the `csv_escape` helper defined immediately below it. Any field value containing a comma, a double quote, or a newline will change the column/record boundaries of the generated document — a consumer parsing the output sees extra columns or extra rows that the producer never intended. If `rows` originates from user-supplied report data (the entry point is not visible in this diff or in the retrieved context), this is field/record injection into the CSV consumer.

Fix: render each field via `csv_escape(str(r.get(c, "")))`, and extend `csv_escape` to also quote values containing `\n` or `\r` (the current predicate on line 12 only covers `,` and `"`). Using the stdlib `csv` module would handle all of this. Separately, consider prefixing values beginning with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` if the output is opened in a spreadsheet.

findings.title: csv_escape raises TypeError for non-string values
findings.body: `csv_escape` immediately does `"," in value`, which raises `TypeError: argument of type 'int' is not iterable` for any non-string input. Report cells are frequently numbers, dates or `None`. Either coerce at the top (`value = str(value)`) or document that callers must pass strings — the docstring currently says only "a value", implying any value is acceptable.

findings.title: dump_streaming yields nothing for an empty rows list
findings.body: When `rows` is empty, `range(0, 0, chunk_size)` is empty and the generator yields no chunks at all, so a consumer writing the stream to a file produces a zero-byte output rather than a valid `[]`. `dump([])` by contrast returns `"[]"`. If callers treat the two functions as interchangeable, the empty-report case differs. Consider yielding `"[]"` when `rows` is empty. Note also that `len(rows)` and slicing require a sequence, so this cannot stream a generator despite the name.

findings.title: New test relies on real datetime.now(), reintroducing time-dependent flakiness
findings.body:
The existing test (line 4-6) deliberately fixes 'now' via an explicit `now=` argument to avoid time dependence — exactly the pattern this PR's title suggests we're testing for. The new test instead calls `issue_token()` and `is_expired(token.expires_at)` with no fixed time, and compares `token.issued_at.date()` to `datetime.now(timezone.utc).date()`. If `issue_token()` and the assertion straddle midnight UTC, or if the test runs in CI at exactly that boundary, the date comparison fails spuriously despite correct behaviour — the opposite of what a 'test the token expiry window' PR should add.

_Also raised by the correctness agent:_ Date comparison against datetime.now() is flaky across UTC midnight

findings.title: No test covers the expired-coupon rejection path
findings.body: apply_coupon now raises CouponExpired when coupon.expires_at is in the past, but the only test updated (test_apply_coupon_reduces_total) uses a coupon with expires_at=tomorrow(), which never exercises this branch. If the comparison logic were inverted, or the exception were never raised, or raised for valid coupons, no test would fail. Add a test that passes an already-expired coupon and asserts CouponExpired is raised.

findings.title: apply_coupon can now raise; existing callers assume it always returns an order
findings.body: `apply_coupon` previously always returned the mutated order. It can now raise `CouponExpired` on a reachable input (any coupon past its expiry). Every existing call site that treats the return value as unconditional \u2014 e.g. checkout paths that do `order = apply_coupon(order, coupon)` \u2014 will now propagate an uncaught exception instead of completing. Either catch `CouponExpired` at the call sites and surface a user-facing validation error, or return a result/None the callers already handle. No call sites were included in the diff or retrieved context, so this needs verification against the rest of the codebase.

findings.title: Public function `apply_coupon` lacks contract documentation for new exception
findings.body: The function `apply_coupon` is now a public API that raises `CouponExpired` when a coupon has expired (line 9-10), but there is no docstring documenting this behavior. A caller cannot determine from the function signature alone that they must handle `CouponExpired` or that it requires checking coupon expiration. This is a public contract change that callers need to know about.
